title: Medium to long term follow up study of the efficacy of cessation of eye-rubbing to halt progression of keratoconus

groups.description: 153 eyes of 77 consecutive treatment-naive keratoconus patients aged 12-40 years at the first visit, minimum 3-year follow-up; instructed to stop eye rubbing and monitored without cross-linking or surgery (prior cross-linking or surgery excluded) (Methods, Table 1)

exclusions.reason: time is a range (more than 48 months), not a dated visit

exclusions.what: PMC10244573.xml::tab5 sub-group series (No ARB/RER, RER only, ARB only, ARB & RER)
exclusions.reason: sub-groups defined by at-risk behaviour and eye rubbing reported during follow-up (whether patients stopped), not a pre-treatment condition or protocol; the whole cohort (Table 3) is extracted and the sub-groups would count the same eyes twice
groups selected by a post-treatment outcome (progression)
p-values (each timepoint against the previous one)

exclusions.what: Figures 2A,B (per-eye DeltaKmax at the end of follow-up)
exclusions.reason: figure only and undated final visit; no table cells

notes: Observation context: no cross-linking or ring segment during follow-up; patients were counselled to stop eye rubbing, offered topical antihistamines or lubricants for itch and a rigid night-time eye shield (Methods).
Baseline is the first visit to the centre; follow-up visits at 6 months, 1, 2, 3 years and yearly afterwards (Methods).
Inclusion required a minimum follow-up of 3 years (77 of 176 eligible patients); kept under the protocol because the minimum follow-up is shorter than the last tabulated visit (48 months).
Both eyes of most patients are included (153 eyes of 77 patients).
Kmean (Tables 4, 6), thinnest pachymetry (Tables 7, 8) and sub-group baseline characteristics (Table 2) are tabulated and not used.

series.baseline_label: Kmax at the first visit to the centre (Table 1, all 153 keratoconus eyes)
series.notes: Table 3 mean of DeltaKmax (visit minus baseline) with SD; per-visit N in Table 3 (78 at 6, 107 at 12, 90 at 24, 116 at 36, 72 at 48 months); n is the 153 eyes at baseline; dioptres from the Methods (progression criterion > 1.0 D), no unit in the tables
